questions.question: Who among the following was the pioneer of widow remarriages in Maharashtra and also started a girls' school in Poona along with his wife?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Jyotirao Govindrao Phule**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Jyotirao Govindrao Phule** was a social reformer and activist from Maharashtra who played a crucial role in the promotion of widow remarriages.
 
• He, along with his wife Savitribai Phule, started the first school for girls in Poona (now Pune) in 1848.
 
• Phule's efforts were pioneering in challenging the prevailing caste system and advocating for the rights of the oppressed, including women and lower castes.
 
• His work laid the foundation for subsequent social reform movements in Maharashtra and beyond.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Jyotirao Phule** was born on 11 April 1827 in Satara district, Maharashtra.
 
• He was also the founder of the Satyashodhak Samaj (Society of Truth Seekers), which aimed at achieving social equality.
 
• Phule's literary works include the play "Tritiya Ratna" and the book "Gulamgiri" (Slavery).
 
• His contributions to education and social reform have made him a revered figure in Indian history, particularly in Maharashtra.

questions.question: Who among the following classical poets of the Sultanate period in India popularised Qawwali, a form of music which derived its name from the Arabic word ‘qaul’, meaning ‘to speak’?
questions.solution:

• He was a great musician, scholar, and poet.

• Tabla, Sitar, and Qawwali were invented by Amir Khusro.
 
• Kiran-us-Saden, Mifta-ul-Futuh, Khazain-ul-Futuh, Ashika, and Tughlaqnama are his main books.
 
• **Amir Khusrau was famous as the parrot of Hind.**
 
• His creations are a reflection of Indian social culture not only at the level of sensitivity but also at the level of craft
 
• His real name was Abul Hasan Yaminuddin Muhammad.
 
• **Amir Khusro** was born in 1253 AD in a town named Patiali in Etah (Uttar Pradesh). 
 
• He was given the title of Khusro at the age of just 12 by the scholar Khwaja Ijuddin.
 
• His spiritual guru's name was Nizamuddin Olia, who was famous as Mehboob-e-Ilahi.

• He believed the love of God implied a love of humanity.
 
• He had a major influence on the Muslims of Delhi and the world over.
 
 
 
• **Jalal al-Din Muhammad Rumi - **
 
 
• Rūmī was a great Sufi mystic and poet in the Persian language, famous for his lyrics and for his didactic epic Mas̄navī-yi Maʿnavī (“Spiritual Couplets”), which widely influenced mystical thought and literature throughout the Muslim world.​
 
 
 
• **Shams al-Din Muhammad Hafiz - **
 
 
• Hafez of Shiraz (also given as Hafiz, l. 1315-1390) is considered the greatest of the Persian poets and among the most famous and admired writers in world literature.
 
• He is among the most often translated poets in the present day and his work continues to resonate with modern audiences.

questions.question: The ‘Servants of India Society’ was the brainchild of which of the following leaders?
questions.solution:
​

The correct answer is __**Gopal Krishna Gokhale**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Servants of India Society**, established in **Pune, Maharashtra**, on **June 12, 1905**, by **Gopal Krishna Gokhale,** emerged from** his vision of social reform and national liberation.**
 
• Departing from the **Deccan Education Society, Gokhale** formed this association with a select group of enlightened Indians, including Natesh Appaji Dravid, Gopal Krishna Deodhar, Surendra Nath Banerjee, and Anant Patwardhan.
 
• Their collective mission aimed at fostering social progress and emancipation from British colonial rule.
 
• Through various campaigns, the Society championed causes such as education, sanitation, healthcare, and the eradication of social ills like untouchability, discrimination, alcoholism, and poverty. 
 
• **The publication of The Hitavada,** the Society's English-language organ from Nagpur, commenced in **1911**, serving as a powerful tool for disseminating its message and mobilizing public opinion.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Gopal Krishna Gokhale **was an Indian political leader and social reformer during the Indian independence movement.
 
• He served as the political mentor of Mahatma Gandhi and was a senior leader of the Indian National Congress.
 
• Gokhale founded the Servants of India Society and advocated for Indian self-rule and social reforms.
 
• He led the moderate faction within the Congress party and was a prominent member of the Poona Association or the Poona Sarvajanik Sabha.

• Occasionally called the**" Shahenshah-e-Qawwali"**( the King of lords of Qawwali), he's considered by The New York Times to be the topmost qawwali songster of his generation.
 
• He was described as the fourth topmost songster of all time by LA Weekly in 2016.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Shabad:**

 
 
• Shabad is a word meaning hymn, sacred song, sound, verse, voice, or word. In Sikhism, a Shabad is a sacred song selected from Sikhism's scripture ​ Guru Granth Sahib, everlasting Guru of the Sikhs.
 
 
 
• **Bhatiali:**
 
 
• Bhatiali or bhatiyali is a form of folk music in both Bangladesh and West Bengal. Bhatiali is a swash song substantially sung by boatmen while going down aqueducts of the swash.
 
• The word bhatiyali comes from bhata meaning" eclipse" or downstream.
 
 
 
• **Bhajan:**
 
 
• Bhajan is a Sanskrit word meaning “ singing to glorify God." It's also the name of a Hindu kidney of spiritual songs and hymns.
 
• The term covers a wide range of spiritual music, from a simple mantra to the more complex Hindu dhrupad.

questions.question: Ashtadhyayi, is a Sanskrit treatise on grammar, written in the 6th to 5th century BCE by _________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Panini**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Panini was **an Indian grammarian, who authored the **Ashtadhyayi,** a seminal Sanskrit grammar treatise, during the** 6th to 5th century BCE**.
 
• This comprehensive work offers insights into the language prevalent during Pāṇini's era, encompassing various dialects and registers spoken by an **elite group of individuals**.
 
• It also incorporates elements of the **older Vedic language** alongside contemporary dialectal features.
 
• The Ashtadhyāyī employs a derivational system to elucidate the structure of the language, illustrating how real speech emerges from abstract utterances through the addition of affixes to base forms under specific conditions.
 
• While the exact timeframe of Pāṇini's life remains uncertain, some scholars place him in the **4th century BCE,** coinciding with the era of conquests.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Patanjali,** also known as Gonardiya or Gonikaputra, was a Hindu author, mystic, and philosopher. Scholars estimate that he lived between the 2nd century BCE and the 4th century CE based on analyses of his works.
 
• **Agastya** is a revered Indian sage in Hinduism, renowned as a recluse and influential scholar proficient in various languages of the Indian subcontinent.
 
• **Vishvamitra **is among the most revered rishis, or sages, of ancient India and is recognized as one of the seven Brahmarshis.

questions.question: Guru Bipin Singh, who received the honour of Sangeet Natak Akademi Award in 1966 and the Kalidas Samman from the Madhya Pradesh Government, was an exponent of which of the following Indian classical dance forms?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Manipuri**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Guru Bipin Singh** (1918 - 2000) was a luminary in the realm of **Manipuri dance,** renowned as a director, choreographer, and teacher.
 
• His contributions to the art form were celebrated with the prestigious Sangeet Natak Akademi Award in 1966, the highest honor bestowed upon practicing artists in India.
 
• He was honored with the Kalidas Samman by the Government of Madhya Pradesh. Revered as the Father of Manipuri style, Singh's expertise was cultivated through extensive training under esteemed masters in Manipur and neighboring districts.
 
• Guru Bipin Singh was bestowed with the title of Hanjaba by the Maharaja of Manipur, further testament to his profound impact and esteemed status within the realm of Manipuri dance. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Manipuri dance,** also known as Manipuri Raas Leela, is a form of jagoi and is one of the major Indian classical dance forms, originating from the state of Manipur.
 
• It is one of the greatest cultural achievements of the traditional Vaishnavism adhering Meitei people of Manipur.
 
• Developed by Meitei Hindu king Ching Thang Khomba, it is considered the highest spiritual expression of the worship of Hindu deity Krishna.
 
• Recognized by the Sangeet Natak Akademi as one of the primary classical dance forms of India, it is honored with the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award for Manipuri annually.

questions.question: Who among the following Bahmani sultans transferred his capital from Gulbarga to Bidar?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ahmad Shah**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ahmad Shah I,** the **ninth sultan of the Bahmani Sultanate,** made a significant decision in **1422 **by relocating the **capital from Gulbarga to Bidar**.
 
• This move was motivated by Bidar's strategic advantages, including its more favorable climate and central location.
 
• **Bidar** was surrounded by fertile land and became even more centrally situated after the acquisition of territory to the southeast in Telingana.
 
• Ahmad Shah I's reign heralded the transition from the Gulbarga phase to the Bidar phase of the Bahmani kingdom.
 
• Under his rule, the **Bahmani Sultanate **experienced a shift in focus towards expansionism and military campaigns.
 
• Ahmad Shah I converted to Shi'ism, marking a religious change within the ruling elite.
 
• His reign was characterized by efforts to strengthen and expand the kingdom's territories, setting the stage for significant developments in the Bahmani Sultanate's history.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

__
 
• **Ahmad Shah I, **originally known as Ahmad Khan, was a significant ruler of the Muzaffarid dynasty, governing the **Gujarat Sultanate from 1411** until his passing in 1442.
 
• He was the grandson of Sultan Muzaffar Shah, the dynasty's founder.
 
• Ahmad Shah I is renowned as the founder of Ahmedabad, the most populous city in Gujarat, which bears his name.
 
• Besides his administrative accomplishments, he was also a notable poet, having composed a collection of Persian poetry.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Humayun,** the second Mughal emperor, ruled over vast territories spanning Eastern Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Northern India, and Pakistan from 1530 to 1540 and again from 1555 until his death in 1556.
 
• **Mujahid Shah Bahmani **ascended to the throne as the 3rd Sultan of the Bahmani Sultanate, playing a significant role in its governance and development.
 
• **Sultan Firuz Shah Tughlaq,** hailing from the Tughlaq dynasty, was a prominent Muslim ruler who reigned over the Sultanate of Delhi from 1351 to 1388, leaving a lasting impact on the region's history and administration.

questions.question: Ustad Asad Ali Khan is famous for which of the following schools of Dhrupad as an instrumentalist?

questions.question: In 2015, the eminent danseuse and ______________ exponent, Padma Subrahmanyam was selected for Kerala's prestigious choreography award 'Nishagandhi Puraskaram' instituted by the state tourism department.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bharatanatyam**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **2015, Padma Subrahmanyam, **a renowned danseuse and **Bharatanatyam **exponent, was honored with **Kerala's** prestigious choreography award, the **'Nishagandhi Puraskaram,' **established by the state tourism department.
 
• This recognition reflects her exceptional contributions to the field of dance and choreography. Padma **Subrahmanyam's mastery of Bharatanatyam,** a classical Indian dance form, has earned her widespread acclaim and admiration.
 
• Her innovative choreography and dedication to preserving and promoting Indian classical dance traditions have made her a trailblazer in the field.
 
• The 'Nishagandhi Puraskaram' award acknowledges her outstanding artistic achievements and serves to celebrate her profound impact on the cultural landscape of India.
 
• Padma Subrahmanyam was honored with the **Padma Vibhushan in 2024,** the **Padma Bhushan in 2003, **and the **Padma Shri in 1981**, prestigious civilian awards of India, which rank among the highest recognitions bestowed by the nation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Bharatanatyam**, a classical Indian dance form originating in **Tamil Nadu,** stands as the most widely recognized classical dance style in India.
 
• Known for its precise movements, crisp lines, and expressive gestures, Bharatanatyam embodies the rich cultural heritage of South India.
 
• The dance form serves as a vehicle for conveying religious themes and spiritual concepts, particularly those associated with Shaivism and Hinduism in general.
 
• Traditionally performed as a collaborative art form, Bharatanatyam features a solo dancer accompanied by musicians and one or more vocalists.
 
• It encompasses a diverse range of themes, including religious narratives, secular subjects, and fusion styles that blend traditional and contemporary elements.

questions.question: Jagjit Singh is associated with which form of singing?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ghazal**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Jagjit Singh**, renowned as the** "Ghazal King," **is celebrated for his association with ghazals, a **classical Persian song** form known for its **special rhyming patterns and stanzas** conveying themes of love.
 
• Credited with revitalizing the popularity of ghazals, Singh's work is considered genre-defining, making him the most successful ghazal singer and composer of all time.
 
• In recognition of his contributions, he was honored with the **Padma Bhushan** by the Government of India in 2003.
 
• Additionally, in February 2014, the government released a set of two postal stamps in his honor.
 
• Notably, Singh's rendition of Bahadur Shah Zafar's famous ghazal "Lagta nahin hai dil mera" at an event commemorating the 150th anniversary of the Indian Rebellion of 1857, held in the Central Hall of the Parliament of India on May 10, 2007, captivated audiences comprising numerous political and diplomatic luminaries.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The ghazal** is a **form of amatory poem or ode,** with its origins rooted in **Arabic poetry.**
 
• Typically, ghazals delve into themes of spiritual and romantic love, serving as a poetic expression of the complexities inherent in love, including the pain of separation from the beloved juxtaposed with the beauty of enduring love.
 
• Dating back to 7th-century Arabic poetry, the ghazal has a rich and ancient history.
 
• It found its way into the Indian subcontinent during the 12th century, influenced by Sufi mystics and the courts of the new Islamic Sultanate.

questions.question: Who among the following is related to the Lucknow Kalka-Bindadin gharana of Kathak?

• Birju Maharaj was a philanthropist of the** Padma Vibhushan, India's second highest civilian honor, in 1986.**

questions.question: Who among the following leaders founded the women’s wing of Congress in 1940?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sucheta Kriplani**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Sucheta Kriplani was **among the freedom fighters who founded the **women's wing of Congress** in 1940.
 
• Sucheta Kripalani was India's inaugural female Chief Minister, leading the Uttar Pradesh government from 1963 to 1967.
 
• Like her contemporaries Aruna Asaf Ali and Usha Mehta, she rose during the Quit India Movement and faced arrest by the British.
 
• She later collaborated closely with Mahatma Gandhi during the Partition riots, accompanying him to Noakhali in 1946.
 
• She was among the few women elected to the Constituent Assembly of India and served as the first woman CM of Uttar Pradesh from the Kanpur constituency. Additionally, she was part of the subcommittee that drafted the Indian Constitution.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] 

**Important Points__**

__
 
• **The All India Mahila Congress (AIMC),** also known as Mahila Congress, serves as the women's division of the Indian National Congress (INC), established in 1940 with the aim of advancing the political and social empowerment of women across India.
 
• Currently, Alka Lamba holds the position of president of the All India Mahila Congress, assuming office on January 5, 2024.
 
• The AIMC operates through regional branches known as Pradesh Mahila Congress (State Women's Congress), which represent the AIMC in various states and union territories of India.
 
• These Pradesh Mahila Congress units are responsible for overseeing the affairs of AIMC within their respective regions. Membership in AIMC is comprised of women who are card-carrying members of the Indian National Congress. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Lakshmi Sahgal **was a key figure in the Indian independence movement, serving as an officer in the Indian National Army and later as the Minister of Women's Affairs in the Azad Hind government.
 
• **Sarojini Naidu,** renowned as both a political activist and poet, made history as the first Governor of the United Provinces following India's independence.
 
• **Aruna Asaf Ali**, an educator, political activist, and publisher, played a pivotal role in the Indian independence movement. She is best remembered for her courageous act of hoisting the Indian National flag at the Gowalia Tank maidan in Bombay during the Quit India Movement of 1942.

questions.question: Who among the following was the first president of IOC?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Demetrius Vikelas**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Demetrius Vikelas (1805–1908)** served as the inaugural president of the **International Olympic Committee (IOC)** from 1894 to 1896, holding the distinction of having the shortest tenure among all IOC presidents, **spanning just two years.**
 
• A Greek businessman and writer, Vikelas **co-founded the IOC **alongside Pierre de Coubertin in 1894.
 
• In addition to his involvement in sports administration, Vikelas made significant contributions to education.
 
• In **1893, **he established the Institut Melas, an institution dedicated to providing preschool education in regions of Greece beyond Athens.
 
• Vikelas is often characterized as the most cosmopolitan, internationally-minded, and erudite president in the history of the IOC.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

__
 
• The International Olympic Committee (IOC), a non-governmental sports organization, is responsible for organizing the **modern Olympic Games,** which occur every two years, alternating between the summer and winter editions.
 
• The president of the IOC typically serves two terms of four years each, with the possibility of renewal once, allowing them to oversee at least two Summer and two Winter Olympic Games during their tenure.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Michael Morris**, 3rd Baron Killanin, was an Irish journalist, author, sports official, and the sixth President of the International Olympic Committee.
 
• **Pierre de Coubertin, **also known as Baron de Coubertin, was a French educator and historian, renowned as the co-founder of the International Olympic Committee and its second president. He is widely regarded as the father of the modern Olympic Games.
 
• **Avery Brundage** was an American sports administrator who held the position of the fifth president of the International Olympic Committee from 1952 to 1972.

questions.question: Hara Shankar Bhattacharya is a maestro of ___________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**sitar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Pandit Harashankar Bhattacharya** is a renowned **sitar maestro, **widely regarded as one of **India's foremost sitarists.**
 
• His musical journey has been marked by prestigious performances on** All India Radio (AIR)** and television as an **"A-TOP" artist.**
 
• Additionally, he has collaborated with the esteemed **Shri Ram Bharatiya Kala Kendra in Delhi.**
 
• Following his relocation to Kolkata, Bhattacharya assumed the role of the Government of West Bengal's senior sitarist in Information and Cultural Affairs.
 
• Born into a musical lineage, he inherited his passion for music from his grandfather, the esteemed** "Sitari" Lalmohon Bhattacharya.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The sitar, **a plucked stringed instrument native to the Indian subcontinent, belongs to the lute family.
 
• Primarily featured in Hindustani classical music, this genre is distinguished by intricate rhythmic structures, ornate melodies, and extensive improvisation.
 
• Measuring approximately 4 feet (1.2 meters) in length, the sitar typically features a pear-shaped gourd body and a lengthy, broad, hollow wooden neck.

questions.question: Pandit Ravi Shankar popularised which instrument in particular all over the world?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sitar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Pandit Ravi Shankar **is renowned for popularizing the sitar, an Indian stringed instrument, globally. Shankar was a virtuoso of the sitar, an intricate instrument with a captivating resonance.
 
• Born on April 7, 1920, he commenced his performing career at the age of 14 as a dancer in his brother Uday's ensemble.
 
• Throughout the latter half of the 20th century, he ascended to become the foremost ambassador of North Indian classical music on the global stage.
 
• Shankar's artistic oeuvre encompasses a diverse range of endeavors, from composing pieces for orchestras to fusing clarinets with traditional Indian melodies, and even imparting sitar lessons to George Harrison, the guitarist of the Beatles.
 
• Additionally, he is the father of the acclaimed singer-songwriter Norah Jones.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The term **"sitar" **originates from the Persian word "sehtar," translating to "three-stringed." Believed to have evolved from long-necked lutes brought to India from Central Asia, the sitar reached its pinnacle during the 16th and 17th centuries before attaining its current form in the 18th century.
 
• **Tabla** comprises a pair of hand drums indigenous to the Indian subcontinent.
 
• **The veena** encompasses various chordophone instruments native to the Indian subcontinent.
 
• **Harmonium** resembles an organ and operates as a portable, hand-pumped reed organ, finding popularity across the Indian subcontinent.

questions.question: Soparrkar and the logo of his worldwide initiative ‘Dance for a Cause’ are being printed on an official postage stamp issued by the _______________ government.

__
 
• **Soparrkar and the logo **of his worldwide initiative **‘Dance for a Cause’ **are being printed on an** official postage stamp **issued by the **Bhutan government.**
 
• This recognition of Soparrkar and his initiative "Dance for a Cause" through the issuance of an official postage stamp by the Bhutan government is a notable acknowledgment of their contribution to the world of dance and their philanthropic endeavors.
 
• The **decision to feature **Soparrkar and his initiative on a postage stamp signifies their significant impact and influence, both within Bhutan and globally.
 
• It showcases the government's appreciation for their efforts in promoting dance as a form of expression and their commitment to social causes.
 
• Furthermore, being featured on a postage stamp adds prestige and visibility to Soparrkar's work, as stamps are often considered symbols of honor and recognition.
 
• It also serves as a means of promoting their cause to a wider audience, as stamps are circulated through mail services and can reach people across different regions and demographics.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sandip Soparrkar** is an acclaimed Indian Latin and ballroom dancer, renowned TEDx speaker, and scholar with a doctorate in **World Mythology Folklore from the Pacifica Graduate Institute** in the United States.
 
• He holds an Honorary Doctorate in Performing Arts from The National American University. His remarkable contributions to the field of dance and culture have earned him numerous accolades, including three National Excellence Awards and one National Achievement Award bestowed upon him by the Government of India.
 
• Soparrkar's endeavors have also been recognized internationally, as he has been honored with the Rabindranath Tagore Literary Prize for Social Achievement. Furthermore, his dedication to the arts has been acknowledged with prestigious awards such as the Bharat Gaurav Samaan presented by the Ministry of Culture at The House of Lords in London, UK.
 
• He is a recipient of the esteemed Shakti Samman, symbolized by a sword, conferred upon him by the Ministry of Culture, Government of India.
